subproblem.title: Mean-value bounds for difference quotients on ball(xb, 2R)
subproblem.statement: Let E and F be real normed spaces, α a real number, U ⊆ E open, g : E → F differentiable on U, xb, e ∈ E and R, S, H, d real numbers with closedBall(xb, 4R) ⊆ U, ‖e‖ ≤ 1, d ≠ 0 and |d| < R. Assume ‖Dg(z)‖ ≤ S for all z ∈ closedBall(xb, 4R) and ‖Dg(z) − Dg(w)‖ ≤ H‖z − w‖^α for all z, w ∈ closedBall(xb, 4R), where Dg = fderiv ℝ g. Then for all x, y in the open ball ball(xb, 2R): (a) ‖d⁻¹(g(x + d e) − g(x))‖ ≤ S, and (b) ‖d⁻¹(g(x + d e) − g(x)) − d⁻¹(g(y + d e) − g(y))‖ ≤ H‖x − y‖^α.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (E F : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (α : ℝ) (U : Set E) (g : E → F) (xb e : E) (R S H d : ℝ), IsOpen U → closedBall xb (4 * R) ⊆ U → ‖e‖ ≤ 1 → DifferentiableOn ℝ g U → (∀ z ∈ closedBall xb (4 * R), ‖fderiv ℝ g z‖ ≤ S) → (∀ z ∈ closedBall xb (4 * R), ∀ w ∈ closedBall xb (4 * R), ‖fderiv ℝ g z - fderiv ℝ g w‖ ≤ H * ‖z - w‖ ^ α) → d ≠ 0 → |d| < R → ∀ x ∈ ball xb (2 * R), ∀ y ∈ ball xb (2 * R), ‖d⁻¹ • (g (x + d • e) - g x)‖ ≤ S ∧ ‖d⁻¹ • (g (x + d • e) - g x) - d⁻¹ • (g (y + d • e) - g y)‖ ≤ H * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4, 5 and 6 of the parent proof (geometry, and the difference-quotient lemma for the scalar components and for v). Here they are stated for any g that is differentiable on U and has the given derivative bounds. Notation: K0 := closedBall(xb, 4R), B := ball(xb, 2R), Dg = fderiv ℝ g.
1. Preliminaries. Since d ≠ 0, |d| > 0. Since 0 ≤ |d| < R, R > 0. K0 is convex (convex_closedBall).
2. Geometry. Let z ∈ B and s ∈ ℝ with |s| ≤ |d|. Then ‖(z + s e) − xb‖ = ‖(z − xb) + s e‖ ≤ ‖z − xb‖ + |s| ‖e‖ ≤ 2R + |d| · 1 ≤ 2R + R ≤ 4R, using ‖z − xb‖ < 2R, ‖e‖ ≤ 1 and |d| < R. Hence z + s e ∈ K0 ⊆ U. In particular z ∈ K0 (take s = 0) and z + d e ∈ K0 (take s = d).
3. Differentiability on K0. If z ∈ K0 then z ∈ U. Since U is open it is a neighbourhood of z (IsOpen.mem_nhds). g is differentiable within U at z, so g is differentiable at z (DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt), with derivative Dg(z).
4. Part (a). Let x ∈ B. By step 2, x ∈ K0 and x + d e ∈ K0. By step 3, g is differentiable at every point of the convex set K0, and ‖Dg‖ ≤ S on K0. So the mean value inequality Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le gives ‖g(x + d e) − g(x)‖ ≤ S ‖(x + d e) − x‖ = S |d| ‖e‖. Also S ≥ ‖Dg(x)‖ ≥ 0, so S |d| ‖e‖ ≤ S |d|. Therefore ‖d⁻¹ • (g(x + d e) − g(x))‖ = |d|⁻¹ ‖g(x + d e) − g(x)‖ ≤ S, by norm_smul, norm_inv and inv_mul_le_iff₀ with |d| > 0.
5. Part (b), setup. Let x, y ∈ B and let I := uIcc 0 d, the closed interval between 0 and d. I is convex (convex_uIcc), and 0, d ∈ I (Set.left_mem_uIcc, Set.right_mem_uIcc). Let h(s) := g(x + s e) − g(y + s e). For s ∈ I we have |s| ≤ |d|: if 0 ≤ d then 0 ≤ s ≤ d, and if d ≤ 0 then d ≤ s ≤ 0. Hence, by step 2, x + s e and y + s e lie in K0.
6. Part (b), derivative of h. For every s, the map σ ↦ x + σ e has derivative e at s (((hasDerivAt_id s).smul_const e).const_add x), and likewise for y. For s ∈ I, step 3 and the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) show that σ ↦ g(x + σ e) has derivative Dg(x + s e) e at s, and similarly for y. So h has derivative h'(s) := Dg(x + s e) e − Dg(y + s e) e at s (HasDerivAt.sub), and in particular within I (HasDerivAt.hasDerivWithinAt).
7. Part (b), bound on h'. For s ∈ I,
   ‖h'(s)‖ = ‖(Dg(x + s e) − Dg(y + s e)) e‖
     ≤ ‖Dg(x + s e) − Dg(y + s e)‖ ‖e‖   (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm)
     ≤ ‖Dg(x + s e) − Dg(y + s e)‖   (‖e‖ ≤ 1)
     ≤ H ‖(x + s e) − (y + s e)‖^α = H ‖x − y‖^α.
   The last line uses the Hölder hypothesis at the two points of K0 from step 5 and (x + s e) − (y + s e) = x − y.
8. Part (b), conclusion. Apply the mean value inequality on the convex set I (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasDerivWithin_le), with the derivative from step 6, the bound from step 7 and endpoints 0 and d. It gives ‖h(d) − h(0)‖ ≤ H ‖x − y‖^α ‖d − 0‖ = H ‖x − y‖^α |d|. Since 0 • e = 0, h(0) = g(x) − g(y). So d⁻¹ • (g(x + d e) − g(x)) − d⁻¹ • (g(y + d e) − g(y)) = d⁻¹ • (h(d) − h(0)), by smul_sub and rearranging in the abelian group. Its norm is |d|⁻¹ ‖h(d) − h(0)‖ ≤ H ‖x − y‖^α.
9. Steps 4 and 8 give the two claimed inequalities for all x, y ∈ B. QED
proof_key_steps: geometry: z ∈ ball(xb, 2R), |s| ≤ |d| < R and ‖e‖ ≤ 1 give z + s e ∈ closedBall(xb, 4R) ⊆ U
g is differentiable at every point of the convex K0 because U is open
(a) mean value inequality on K0 between x and x + d e, then divide by |d|
(b) h(s) = g(x + s e) − g(y + s e) on uIcc 0 d has ‖h'(s)‖ ≤ H‖x − y‖^α; apply the mean value inequality and divide by |d|

audit.reason: All hypotheses and conclusions match. Geometry keeps both translated paths inside the derivative-control set. The proof derives R > 0 and the needed S ≥ 0, handles either sign of d through uIcc 0 d, applies the vector-valued mean-value inequality, and divides by positive |d|. No extra sign assumption on H is needed.
